title: Believing Everything Online
text:
Many people read news on social media every day. Sometimes a post looks true, but it is not. This is called fake news. Fake news can spread very fast because people share it before they check it.

Some fake posts use a photo from an old event. Others use a title that is shocking to get more clicks. Before you share a story, you should read the whole article. You can also check the story on a trusted news website.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why does fake news spread quickly?
options: Because people share it before they check it
Because newspapers print it every day
Because it is always on television

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do some fake posts use?
options: A photo from an old event
A video from a new movie

questions.text: Why might a writer use a very shocking title for a fake post?
options: To show that the newspaper is honest
To help readers check the facts
To make people click and read it

questions.text: What is the best advice from the passage?
options: Trust every photo you see online
Share stories quickly so others see them first
Read the whole article and check the story before you share it

vocabulary.definition: to move or go to many people
believed to be honest and reliable
a piece of writing in a newspaper or on a website

paragraph_translations: Muchas personas leen noticias en las redes sociales todos los días. A veces una publicación parece verdadera, pero no lo es. Esto se llama noticia falsa. Las noticias falsas pueden difundirse muy rápido porque la gente las comparte antes de verificarlas.

Algunas publicaciones falsas usan una foto de un evento antiguo. Otras usan un título tan impactante para conseguir más clics. Antes de compartir una historia, debes leer el artículo completo. También puedes verificar la historia en un sitio web de noticias de confianza.
